# 8-Week Marathon Training Plan Overview

## Plan Strategy
This 8-week plan bridges the critical 13-week gap before your June 15, 2026 marathon target. As an intermediate runner with 1 year of training history, this plan focuses on building running-specific endurance while maintaining strength and mobility through your available gym equipment.

## Key Principles
- **Running Focus (80%)**: Marathon-specific aerobic development with long runs progressing strategically
- **Strength & Conditioning (20%)**: 2 sessions weekly using barbell, dumbbells, kettlebells to prevent injury and maintain power
- **Periodization**: 3 distinct phases aligned with marathon preparation demands
- **Schedule Optimization**: Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat structure allows clustering of harder workouts with recovery days

## Training Week Structure
- **Monday**: Tempo run or speed work (strength day paired)
- **Tuesday**: Long run or steady-state aerobic work
- **Wednesday**: Interval training or fartlek (paired with strength circuit)
- **Thursday**: Rest or easy cross-training
- **Friday**: Rest or mobility work
- **Saturday**: Long run or progressive run (strength session following)
- **Sunday**: Complete rest

## Expected Outcomes
By week 8, you will have:
- Established aerobic base suitable for marathon demands
- Achieved progressive long run distances (peak ~30-32km equivalent stimulus)
- Maintained muscular strength and power through bi-weekly gym sessions
- Developed mental toughness for race-day demands
- Built sufficient fitness to enter final 5-week peak training phase

## Important Notes
- No current injuries/limitations allows for progressive loading
- Baseline fitness not measured; conservative progression recommended
- Adjust paces based on perceived exertion and heart rate monitoring
- Strength sessions should complement running, not compete with it
- Post-week 8, you'll transition into final 5-week peak and taper phase (external to this plan)

## Volume Progression
- **Week 1-2**: Foundation building (50-55 km running volume)
- **Week 3-4**: Volume increase (60-70 km running volume)
- **Week 5-6**: Peak base phase (75-85 km running volume)
- **Week 7-8**: Pre-build taper (65-70 km running volume, shift to intensity)

phase_breakdown.description: Establish foundational endurance capacity and running consistency. Implement 5-day structure with 3 dedicated running sessions (long run, tempo run, easy run). Introduce bi-weekly full-body strength circuits to develop running-specific power and injury resilience. Long runs progress from 18km → 22km. Emphasis on building aerobic base with zone 2 training (easy conversational pace). Strength sessions use compound movements (squats, deadlifts, pull-ups) with 3-4 sets, moderate intensity. Focus on movement quality and consistency of training.

Increase training intensity and volume while maintaining injury prevention through strength work. Long runs progress from 24km → 28km with tempo variations included. Introduce structured speed work: fartlek runs and interval training (5x3min, 3x5min format) on Wednesday. Tuesday becomes dedicated long run day with progressive pace increases. Strength work shifts to 4-6 rep ranges on Olympic lifts and compound movements to build power-endurance. Include running-specific core and stability work (planks, single-leg exercises with kettlebells). Running volume peaks 75-85km/week by week 6.

Begin strategic volume reduction while maintaining intensity for fitness consolidation. Long runs moderate to 28-30km with race-pace segments introduced. Reduce overall run frequency slightly but keep intensity high: tempo runs at marathon pace effort, short intervals at 5K pace. This prepares neuromuscular system for final 5-week peak phase. Strength training becomes more explosive and race-specific: lighter loads with speed emphasis, plyometrics (box jumps with kettlebells), explosive pull-ups. Emphasis on movement efficiency and power maintenance. Running volume 65-70km/week. Mental preparation focus increases; practice race pacing and nutrition strategies.
